Subject: Question on 'temporary egress' trigger in the DPA

Hi Logan / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft earlier. Our legal team flagged section 5.2 — the "temporary egress" carveout that allows cross-region processing for incident response and short-term failover. They asked for two clarifications: 1) what operational conditions constitute an "egress trigger" (is it load, availability, incident, maintenance?), and 2) whether subprocessor roster and telemetry will reflect any transient hops out of the EU for audit purposes.

Attached is our redline (DPA_Acme_v3_redlined.pdf). We use a strict EU anchoring requirement for customer data; a limited temporary exception is acceptable if it is tightly bounded and visible in logs. Can Redwood outline the guardrails and notification windows you propose? Also please confirm whether an escrow or notification to our security contact is required before any failover that crosses borders.

Appreciate a short answer and an ops runbook example.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Security, Acme Payments

Samantha — thanks for the clear redlines and the ask. Quick reply while I loop in ops and legal: we can support a strict EU anchoring posture with a documented transient-egress exception for three defined scenarios: (a) regional outage where capacity in-region is unavailable for >15 minutes despite autoscaling, (b) emergency security remediation that requires hitting a different region to preserve availability, and (c) customer-approved maintenance windows where the customer has pre-authorized transient hops.

For each scenario we propose:
- telemetry logging of any transient egress event (timestamp, source region, destination region, affected model/version, tokens processed)
- automatic notification to the security contact within 30 minutes of any unscheduled transient egress; a 24h notice for scheduled maintenance windows
- a hard cap of 72 hours continuous cross-region processing without an explicit legal escalation and approval

I'm attaching our internal runbook excerpt (runbook_region_pin.xlsx) which shows the telemetry fields and the notification flow. I'll follow up with a more formal legal response and propose concrete DPA language for the carveout.

Pinged Marissa and Kimberly for legal/contract language.

Thanks,
Logan

Folks — looping legal (Kim) and product (Soojin) for a tight answer to Acme. Proposed edits to the DPA: make the carveout conditional on:
1) explicit definition of "egress trigger" limited to: regional infrastructure failure (P1 outage), security-driven containment remediation, or customer pre-approved maintenance;
2) mandatory audit trace emitted to the customer's audit log with the fields Logan listed;
3) maximum continuous transient egress window = 72 hours unless extended via signed SOW/Change Order;
4) require active notification to both security@acme-payments.com and their appointed data steward within 30 minutes for unscheduled events;
5) subcontractor transparency: any subprocessors used for the transient hop must be listed in the subprocessor roster within 48 hours of the event and included in a follow-up DPA addendum if they persist beyond 7 days.

Kim — can legal convert the above to DPA clause text and confirm whether an escrow/escrow-trigger mechanism is necessary, or if the notification + log trail is sufficient? Suggest we avoid escrow unless legal advises it's required for Acme's compliance posture.

Samantha — team has reviewed and we can propose the following DPA language and operational commitments as a package. High level summary first, then the proposed clause text attached.

High level commitments:
- EU anchoring by default: customer data will be processed and stored in the EU unless explicitly pinned otherwise.
- Transient Egress Triggers (only three allowed): (i) regional P1 outage confirmed by monitoring, (ii) security containment or remediation actions required to protect availability/confidentiality, (iii) scheduled maintenance pre-authorized by customer.
- Observability: every transient egress event will emit an audit record to the customer's dedicated telemetry stream with the fields: event_id, start_ts, end_ts, source_region, destination_region, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, subprocessors_used.
- Notification windows: unscheduled events — notify security contact within 30 minutes; scheduled maintenance — 24h prior notice.
- Timebox: 72-hour continuous cross-region processing cap; extension only via written approval (SOW/change order).
- Subprocessor disclosure: transient subprocessors will be disclosed within 48 hours; if they remain in the processing path beyond 7 days a DPA addendum and subprocessor attestation will be required.
- Escrow: Redwood will not require cryptographic escrow in normal operation. If Acme's compliance requires escrow of keys or other custody, we will treat that as an addendum request and provide options (KMS integration/escrow partners) in a separate commercial addendum.

Attached is the draft DPA paragraph (we've inserted precise definitions and the audit schema). If that meets Acme's needs we can push a DocuSign iterate and sync with procurement.
